chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ahmad, Ahmad ibn Muhammad, Nadr ibn Ishaq, al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man, al-Haytham ibn Hammad, Dawud, and Zayd ibn Arqam, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no servant who treats his brother with kindness for the sake of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, in any manner of kindness, except that Allah will have Him serve him from the servants of Paradise.'

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: His brother (referring to a fellow believer)
key_terms.أَخْدَمَهُ: He will serve him / provide service to him
key_terms.فِي اللَّهِ: For the sake of Allah / in devotion to Allah
key_terms.لَطَفَ: To treat with gentleness, kindness, or softness

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for treating a fellow believer with kindness for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the tangible spiritual reward of *lutf* (gentleness) in brotherhood, a core virtue in Shia ethics for strengthening communal bonds. The promise of 'servants of Paradise' serving the believer signifies a high degree of divine honor and ease in the afterlife, reflecting the principle that social kindness is an act of worship. This narration underscores that interpersonal gentleness is not merely social etiquette but a means to attain specific celestial privileges.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  The  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “One  who  loves  his brother  in  any  way,  Allah  will  order  the  servants  from Paradise to serve him.”
